text:
sasha: Heads-up — bringing Llama3-small into the quant pipeline (int8/qlora path). Quick smoke passed but evals show weird token drift for long-contexts. suspect rotary offset + vocab aliasing.
kevin: Can you paste an example where it diverges? short snippet is fine.
sasha: minimal repro: prompt + continuation diverges at 512+ tokens, earlier fine. Perplexity jump from 12 -> 48 around token 520.
sasha: here's the debug print I added in kv cache mapping:
```
input_ids: [101, 3452, 78, 9001, 4002, ...]
kv_pos_index: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, ...]
rotary_phase_index_from_model: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, ...]
rotary_phase_index_computed: [0, 1, 2, 3, 5, ...]  # note jump at pos 4
```
kevin: that jump looks like an off-by-one in the tokenizer->pos mapping. Are we using the Llama3 tokenizer variant (new merges) or a fallback?
sasha: using our standard llama-tokenizer wrapper but loading the shipped vocab.json from the model tar. I dumped token bytes and some tokens have multiple byte sequences that map to same id in our onnx export.
maya: hmm — could be two separate issues: 1) rotary/pos index derivation (cos/sin table) and 2) token id aliasing after export/convert step. We saw similar with Gemma import but this feels different.
ryan: CI bot reports model-conversion step used the older tokenizer config (tokenizer_config.json missing "add_prefix_space": true). That can change the tokenization boundaries and shift rotary positions.
ci-bot: pipeline/convert-llama3-1860543000 completed with warnings: missing tokenizer_config.json, fallback to classic.
kevin: ok that explains boundary shift. But why the phase index jump? that computed index should be pure sequence length. Is there any special handling for BOS token or sentinel tokens insertion?
sasha: I printed seq positions after cleaning special tokens — the gap appears after a multi-byte token that the convert step collapsed into a single id earlier than expected. So the mapping that builds rotary positions uses the length before collapse.
maya: suggestion: recompute rotary_pos using final input_ids length (post-tokenization) rather than original string offsets. quick patch:
```python
# before: pos = char_offset_map[idx]
# after:
pos = enumerate(input_ids)
# ensure cos/sin tables align with len(input_ids)
```
ryan: +1 for recomputing from input_ids. We also need a conversion test: map original tokens -> bytes -> ids and assert roundtrip for tokenizer we ship. Add to convert pipeline.
kevin: adding unit test now. Also adding a small quant smoke that runs a standard prompt with 1024 context and asserts perplexity < 20. Should catch this class of bugs.
sasha: did a quick local patch and re-ran evals — perplexity drop moved from 48 -> 14, long-context samples now match baseline up to 2048. Will push patch shortly.
kevin: also record which tokens were aliased and add a warning in convert step if two byte sequences map to same id (that usually indicates tokenization config mismatch).
maya: note for the notebook: record rotary table generation codepath for Llama3 vs Llama2. there might be slight differences in how rotary dims are interleaved for newer models.
ryan: filed GH issue #2145 (llama3: tokenizer/rotary alignment) and linked the failing eval artifacts.
sasha: link to artifacts: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/llama3/1860543210/ (contains dumps + small repro).
ci-bot: workflow/quant-smoke triggered by kevin unit test — queued on gpu-pool-3. ETA ~18m.
kevin: thanks all. I'll land the convert pipeline test and the rotary-from-inputids patch in the same PR to reduce flakiness.
sasha: one more thing — we should add a small note in onboarding checklist: "verify tokenizer_config present and add_prefix_space parity". lost half an hour to this. :face_with_head_bandage: 
maya: agreed. I'll update the onboarding doc and add a checklist item for: tokenizer roundtrip, rotary table sanity, and quant-smoke.
ryan: can we add a simple grep in package that detects missing tokenizer_config.json and fails convert? prefer fail-fast.
\ekeep: (reaction) :thumbsup:
kevin: will make convert fail on missing config unless explicit override is set. marking as high priority for next deploy.
sasha: PR reference when ready?
kevin: PR 5821 (wip) — pushing tests now.
sasha: great, leaving notes in the eval ticket. thanks team.
